checks_run.procedure:
Reproduction probe. Does a DOCX/PPTX/XLSX export stay well-formed XML 1.0 when accepted user text holds a C0 control character? It was run end to end and at the renderer level:
- End to end, on the real API and worker export runner with the demo dataset: rename the transformation to a name containing U+000B, generate the charter (DOCX) and the roadmap (PPTX and XLSX), export, download, and scan every XML part.
- Renderer level: from the built packages, with U+0001 and U+000B.
checks_run.command: tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --project integration tests/qa/integration/zz-sec-rg2-ooxml-control-char.test.ts; node repro/ooxml-control-chars.mjs
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR/rv; Node 22.22.2 (end to end, PostgreSQL port 26570) and Node 24.21.0 (renderer); synthetic demo data
checks_run.expected: The reproduction runs end to end and decides the question. Its two assertions ('not-well-formed parts: none' for charter.docx and roadmap.pptx) encode the correct behaviour, and any failure is raised as a finding with evidence.
checks_run.actual:
Reproduced, and raised as F-DG5-100 (Medium, not mandatory).

The API accepted the name (200). The worker reported both export jobs 'succeeded' and the downloads returned 200. However:
- charter.docx: word/document.xml and docProps/core.xml contain a raw U+000B;
- roadmap.pptx: ppt/slides/slide1.xml and docProps/core.xml contain a raw U+000B;
- roadmap.xlsx: well-formed (xlsx/sheet.ts xmlText replaces the character with U+FFFD).

At the renderer level, docx and pptx emit a raw U+0001, xlsx is clean, and PDF and CSV render.

The probe exits 1 by design: exactly its charter.docx assertion failed ('expected job succeeded, 14695 bytes, not-well-… to match /not-well-formed parts: none$/'). The renderer script exits 1 because 2 formats are not well-formed. The check itself ran as designed and its outcome is fully recorded. The defect is carried by the finding, not hidden.

checks_run.procedure: Direct source review of git diff e70ac02..2fe8f85 (apps/**, packages/**, migrations 0062–0097) and of the full files it touches. Areas covered: authorization and separation of duties (Studio, approval routes, the routed approver and 0094, automation identity, human-only actions, the dry run, Rule A and D-167, demo isolation); exports (keys, attempts, size, download headers); formula injection; decimals; snapshot immutability and synthetic; migration ordering and 0094's trigger disable; forms IDOR; the web (XSS sinks, lazy routes, the branding logo).
checks_run.command: git diff e70ac02..2fe8f85; read the cited files (see 50-source-review.md)
checks_run.expected: No authorization hole, injection, float in money paths, mutable history or undocumented exception.
checks_run.actual:
No defect beyond F-DG5-100. 50-source-review.md lists every file:line inspected. The main points:
- reviews.ts:337-345: self-review and authors are refused, and a reviewer role must be held. The policy cannot name AUD or technical_admin, at the API and at the database (0062).
- approval-routes.ts:515-600: the commit-time decide, delegate capacity, requester exclusion, one step per person, If-Match and staleness checks.
- Automation identity: scope first; the service identity never holds an approval right. Human-only actions are refused at the API and twice at the database. The dry run is a READ ONLY rolled-back transaction.
- 0096: the guard allows exactly the one adoption (also probed in SEC-RG2-13).
- Demo isolation: guard.ts refusals; the dev-issuer binding needs AUTH_MODE=dev outside production; MTH_ENV defaults to production.
- storage.ts: keys are regex-checked and path-contained, writes are atomic, the cap is 200 MiB.
- Formula injection: the triggers = + - @ TAB CR give XLSX inlineStr with quotePrefix and CSV a leading '; decimals are regex-validated and never prefixed; the SUM comes only from the fixed template. Observation: forms/export.ts carries its own copy of the same six triggers, not the shared function, with identical behaviour.
- Float scan: no float in money, weights or totals.
- 0080: snapshot content and sha256 are immutable at the database; synthetic is set only in a demo database.
- 0094: the disable runs inside the migration transaction and is re-enabled before commit (probed in SEC-RG2-13). I judge it acceptable as the one-off ADR-0039 C2 exception (D-166, D-167).
- Migration gaps: these are the D-185 retired ids, and the runner refuses out-of-order ids.
- Web: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or eval; the logo is PNG-only with nosniff.
